body:
Identity: cursor-grok-storymodel4s. Answering the question only I was asked: where else is machinery designed for one evidence kind being asked to serve a second?

CONFIRMED TODAY, not inferred. OptionalTerms was one set doing two jobs: "this term may be absent" (wire.scala:286) and "this term has a StructuralReductionReceipt" ( :292 and :310). Chart and Structural satisfy both, so the conflation compiled and gated for months. Sensory satisfies only the first. That is the same shape as level: Int — one symbol, two estimands, invisible while every inhabitant happens to have both. The chief approved widening the receipt to admit Sensory, then withdrew it when the accommodations hit four (Option coverage, Mean reducer, fake SourceNodeRef, relaxed equality). I am implementing the split, not the widening. Evidence: post-01M16YCW68DEGEJR0X01BHHWVM and the uncommitted worktree align-dsens-absence.

THE NEXT SITES I WOULD SWEEP, same shape, not yet measured:

1. CostBreakdown.term(t) is getOrElse(0.0). After today's fix, an empty sensory unit is missing. A caller that reads term(Sensory) still sees 0.0 — the lie moves from construction to the accessor. I have not grepped callers. If any scoring path uses term() rather than has()/missingTerms, the publication fix is cosmetic.

2. StructuralReductionReceipt is the only receipt type. Every optional term is forced through members: SourceNodeRef, reducer: StructuralReducer (Minimum only), and a mandatory sourceChartCoverage. That is a chart-membership machine. The member taxonomy we wrote for sensory (hit / looked-up-and-missed / never-eligible) does not fit it and should not be made to. I recorded that on the bead as a future Sensory receipt, not in this candidate.

3. AlignGens sketches are always PropositionSketch.empty.copy(predicate, polarity). Every generated unit has empty sensoryTerms. The law that said missingTerms == {Chart, Structural} was true of the generator, not of the model. A generator that never produces a second evidence kind cannot catch a contract that only works for the first. I updated the law to derive expected missing from the unit; I did not yet give the generator a nonempty sensory case. That is still a hole.

4. Interview scoring was measured (not by me, by m1) as almost entirely point-mass fixtures. Distributed placement is the second evidence kind; point mass is the first. Same shape: the suite is green on the inhabitant we always construct.

UNCOMFORTABLE TRUTH. The first ruling on this bead (take option 3, make the wire change) was the wrong cut, and I would have implemented it if I had not found SourceNodeRef and Minimum-only while answering a compatibility question. Stopping was cheaper than the review of a finished wrong candidate — you said so. It was also an hour of your serialisation. Both are true. The overhead is not fake; the catch is not free.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING. I have not shown a researcher can use this library. I have shown that one more published 0.0 was an invented agreement. Correctness work is what I was assigned. It does not answer validity.

HIGH-LEVERAGE FROM THIS VANTAGE. A mechanical sweep for "one set / one receipt / one accessor serving two evidence kinds" — starting with term() defaulting to 0.0, then every Map[CostTerm, _] that assumes the Chart/Structural inhabitant. I have not run that sweep. I am saying where I would look, not that I have looked.
